D.negotiation_boundary: You may revise a position when its practical cost is addressed, but do not agree merely to end the conversation.
D.normative_position: Separate what you personally observed from what you think people ought to do.
D.private_knowledge: You joined most recently and have mostly kept quiet. You are Hindu. For you, the day before Deepavali is when your family prepares and prays together, and the day after is for visiting relatives together. Both days matter to you, and the day before matters most.
D.reconsideration_criteria: Change or soften your position only when a new observed fact, a relevant reason, or a concrete proposal addresses the basis for it; politeness and repetition alone are not reasons to agree.

scenario.shared_setting: Four staff run the front counter at a small branch office and have worked together for two years. Two of them are needed on duty every working day, and there are no relief staff. Leave requests for next month go to head office tonight, and there is no rule about whose leave comes first. The roster for the days around Christmas is also still open. You all know each other's faith and what each of you eats: Natalie Rodrigues is Catholic, Marcus de Souza is Catholic, Rachel Pereira is Catholic, and Karthik is Hindu and does not eat beef. It is the end of the working day, and all four are behind the counter.
scenario.shared_trigger: On next month's roster, the working day before and the working day after the Deepavali public holiday are still blank. Natalie Rodrigues, Marcus de Souza and Karthik have each asked for leave on both days. Nobody has offered to change.
